text:
alex: Quick sync — ran an A/B on token-trickle chunk sizes + microbatch caps. Short answers: p95 improved with smaller emits, but p99 regressed for long-context requests when KV cache hit-rate was high. Want to understand kernel selector interaction and a safe canary plan.

maya: Can you paste the numbers and which kernels were chosen?

alex: Here are the slices from the perf run (sampled). note: 'trickle' = tokens per flush, microbatch cap = max grouped reqs.
```
config,trickle,microbatch_cap,kv_hit_pct,p95_ms,p99_ms,chosen_kernel
baseline,16,8,45,320,420,kernel_v3_fast
expA,8,8,78,280,540,kernel_v3_fallback
expB,4,4,83,150,610,kernel_v3_fallback
expC,12,8,80,300,480,kernel_v3_fast
```

ryan: That p99 for trickle=4 looks bad despite p95 improving. kernel_v3_fallback spikes — is fallback triggered by seq_len variance or by KV cache state?

alex: From the traces it looks like our kernel selector is using observed peak_seq_len across the microbatch and occasionally re-compiles/chooses a different kernel mid-request when KV cache hits shorten effective seq. Kernel handshake adds ~120–180ms tail in those runs. KV cache evictions also cause a sudden increase in compute.

sophia: Two quick ideas: (1) smooth sequence-length used for kernel selection (moving median over last N requests) so we avoid flip-flopping, (2) increase trickle to 8 for long contexts to reduce kernel renegotiation but that ups first-token perceived latency.

maya: Do we have telemetry for time-to-first-token (TTFT) vs perceived total? product cares about TTFT a lot.

alex: snip from tracer (per-request timeline):
```
REQ 0xabc: recv 0ms | kselect 6ms | kv-lookup 10ms (hit) | enqueue 12ms | compute_start 18ms | first_token 42ms | compute_end 150ms
REQ 0xdef: recv 0ms | kselect 5ms | kv-lookup 300ms (eviction miss) | compile 140ms | first_token 490ms | compute_end 620ms
```
The evictions + compile are the big tail. With trickle=4 we push more emits and more micro-scheduling, which hides TTFT but amplifies chance of hitting the compile path at p99.

perf-bot: perf-test/2160001111 finished. Summary: A/B trickle=8 vs trickle=4. trickle=8 p95=300ms p99=320ms; trickle=4 p95=180ms p99=610ms. KV-hit sessions show worst delta. Details: https://perf.redwood/internal/2160001111

ryan: Proposal: run canary with kernel_selector change -> use median_seq over last 10 requests for pick + cap microbatch_recompile_rate, and set trickle=8 for contexts >1024 tokens. Canary window 2h, sample 5% traffic.

sophia: I'll add feature flags and pin KV cache TTL to reduce mid-canary evictions. Also add a flag to temporarily prefer 'kernel_v3_fast' when median_seq within 10% of fast profile.

maya: watching dashboards :eyes: I'll create alert for p99 increase >20% and TTFT >200ms during canary.

alex: thanks — action items: sophia deploy flags, ryan run canary plan, maya monitor, I'll collect traces. If p99 improvement holds, we'll roll to 25% then 100% with a rollback policy. :thumbsup:
